topic_title: Variational Quantum Algorithms for Constrained Portfolio Optimization

final_report.topic: Variational Quantum Algorithms for Constrained Portfolio Optimization
final_report.title: Benchmarking and Warm-Starting Variational Quantum Algorithms for Constrained Portfolio Optimization

executive_summary.title: Executive Summary
executive_summary.content: Recent research into variational quantum algorithms, specifically the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), demonstrates significant potential as well as notable hurdles when applied to constrained portfolio optimization [cite_exec_1]. Standard parameter initializations on 50-asset Markowitz mean-variance problems hit performance ceilings and barren plateau issues at circuit depths beyond p=4 [cite_exec_1]. Conversely, warm-starting strategies involving the warm-start method which initializes rotation angles using continuous relaxations solved via classical interior-point quadratic programming markedly improve approximation ratios and save optimization iterations on larger asset subsets [cite_exec_2, cite_exec_3].

sections.title: Performance and Limitations of Standard QAOA
sections.content: Benchmarking QAOA on 50-asset Markowitz mean-variance portfolio problems reveals that circuit depths beyond p=4 experience exponential variance suppression due to barren plateaus in random ansatz spaces [cite_1]. Furthermore, standard parameter initialization yields approximation ratios of 0.72 on 27-qubit superconducting hardware, constrained primarily by two-qubit gate error rates of 0.4% [cite_2].

sections.title: Enhancing Performance via Warm-Started QAOA
sections.content: Warm-started QAOA initializes rotation angles using continuous relaxations solved via classical interior-point quadratic programming [cite_3]. On 100-asset S&P 500 subsets, warm-started QAOA achieves an approximation ratio of 0.94 at circuit depth p=2, outperforming greedy classical heuristics while saving 65% of optimization iterations compared to standard random starts [cite_4].

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.content: While standard QAOA implementations face severe hardware noise and barren plateau limitations at deeper circuits [cite_con_1], the warm-start method involves integrating classical continuous relaxations [cite_con_3] to warm-start the optimization process which significantly boosts approximation ratios and saves required optimization iterations [cite_con_2].

limitations: Barren plateaus limit circuit depths beyond p=4 in random ansatz spaces.

Evaluated primarily on subset benchmarks (50-asset Markowitz and 100-asset S&P 500 subsets) rather than full-scale enterprise portfolios.
